differences.title: 1. BATCHING STRATEGY
differences.leftDesc: vLLM uses paged attention to decouple KV cache storage from sequence length. Tokens from many concurrent requests map into a shared, dynamically allocated KV “page” pool, reducing fragmentation and maximizing GPU occupancy.
differences.rightDesc: TGI (Text Generation Inference) performs continuous batching while serving. It groups active sequences into one or more batches, interleaving generation steps to keep the GPU busy, but KV cache layout is less explicitly “paged.”

differences.title: 2. KV CACHE MANAGEMENT
differences.leftDesc: With paged attention, vLLM preallocates KV memory in blocks and grows per request using indirection. This enables stable performance when request lengths diverge, because cache growth doesn’t require moving or re-allocating large contiguous buffers.
differences.rightDesc: TGI’s KV cache is structured around the active batch. As sequences finish or new ones join, cache utilization is managed by rebalancing which sequences stay resident, which can be more sensitive to skewed prompt lengths and workload churn.

differences.title: 3. PARALLELISM & SCALING
differences.leftDesc: vLLM is built around efficient tensor-parallel inference and tight integration with high-throughput decoding. It aims to minimize cross-GPU communication per token by aligning attention and sampling work with partitioned model weights.
differences.rightDesc: TGI supports tensor and pipeline-style sharding patterns via its deployment and backend integration. It focuses on production-friendly scaling for Hugging Face model ecosystems, with routing and batch formation coordinating sharded workers.

differences.title: 4. PERFORMANCE TARGETS
differences.leftDesc: vLLM’s decoding loop prioritizes sustained tokens/sec under contention by leveraging paged KV and scheduling that keeps GPUs saturated. The design often yields higher throughput for mixed-length workloads while maintaining competitive latency.
differences.rightDesc: TGI targets strong serving ergonomics while staying performant for generation workloads. It emphasizes predictable batching behavior, sensible defaults, and operational hooks suited to multi-model and multi-tenant deployments.

differences.title: 5. MODEL COMPATIBILITY PATH
differences.rightDesc: TGI is closely aligned with Hugging Face Transformers models, tokenizers, and model hub conventions. This tight integration reduces friction for deployment, but may constrain advanced scheduler behaviors compared to vLLM’s specialized decoding stack.
differences.leftDesc: vLLM supports a broad range of common open models and inference modes, often with fast iteration on performance features like KV management and decoding kernels. Compatibility typically depends on the model architecture and supported attention implementations.

differences.title: 6. CONTROLS: SAMPLING & DECODING FEATURES
differences.leftDesc: vLLM exposes decoding parameters while optimizing the underlying sampling path for throughput. It can support features like prefix caching and various decoding controls, implemented in ways that respect the paged KV lifecycle.
differences.rightDesc: TGI provides a robust set of API-level generation controls (sampling params, stopping criteria) wired to its batching scheduler. These controls are designed to be predictable in a production server context, including timeouts and request-level limits.

differences.title: 7. OBSERVABILITY & OPERATIONS
differences.leftDesc: vLLM-style deployments tend to surface scheduler-level behavior (effective batching, token throughput, cache utilization) so engineers can tune concurrency, memory limits, and tensor-parallel settings based on live decode dynamics.
differences.rightDesc: TGI commonly integrates with production deployment patterns around the Hugging Face stack: health checks, versioned model loading, and server-level request handling. Operational tuning focuses on concurrency limits and stability under load.
